Question: Which method performs the best when there are a lot of outliers in the data?
Evidence:
[E1] (figure, Figure 6, page 7) (image attached): Figure 6: (a-c) Average ﬁtting errors while varying the outlier rates and (e-f) ﬁtting results of the compared methods with 60% outliers using cosexp , linear , and step functions.
Words printed in the figure: (a) (b) (c) (d) (e) (f)
[E2] (figure, Figure 6, page 7): a zoomed view of Figure 6 (image attached) [image]

claims.text: Figure 6 displays the average fitting errors while varying outlier rates and fitting results of the compared methods.

cites.quote: Figure 6: (a-c) Average ﬁtting errors while varying the outlier rates and (e-f) ﬁtting results of the compared methods with 60% outliers using cosexp , linear , and step functions.

claims.text: Based on the average error plots across different outlier rates, the Proposed method achieves the lowest error when there are many outliers.

cites.observation: In the subplots (a), (b), and (c), the blue solid line representing the Proposed method maintains the lowest average error as the outlier rate increases up to 0.6.
